Summarise an INLAvanilla fit

Source: R/methods.R
summary.inla_vanilla.Rd

Posterior summaries from the skew-normal marginals, on the unconstrained scale of logpost, together with diagnostics of each stage of the approximation.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'inla_vanilla'
summary(object, probs = c(0.025, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.975), ...)

Arguments

object

An object of class inla_vanilla.

probs

Probabilities for the reported quantiles.

...

Unused.

Value

An object of class summary.inla_vanilla: a list with the summary table table, the log marginal likelihood logml (and its Laplace part logml_laplace), the per-parameter diagnostics diagnostics, and details of the optimiser, the VB correction, the number of calls and the timing.

Details

The diagnostics, and the levels at which they are flagged, are:

  • Mode. The largest gradient at the mode in whitened units: how far, in posterior SDs, a Newton step would still move it. The mode is accepted when this is below 0.01, whatever the return code of stats::nlminb(), whose message is shown otherwise.

  • VB correction. The shift of each mean from the mode, in posterior SDs (vb_shift). It is flagged when it exceeds 1 SD, or when the fixed-point iteration failed and the fallback optimiser ran: both mean the posterior is far from the Laplace Gaussian.

  • Tails. Each parameter is scanned over \(\pm 4\) Laplace SDs. tails is FALSE (and flagged) when the density at an end of the scan is still over 5% of its peak: the Laplace SD badly understates a heavy tail there, and the skew-normal extrapolates it.

  • Scan path. bend is the log-density, in nats, that the straight scan misses at \(\pm 2\) posterior SDs: the gain from one Newton step towards the conditional mode of the other parameters. It is flagged above 0.1. A large value means the other parameters' conditional mode bends away from the line, as a poorly determined noise scale does for a regression coefficient at small n, and the marginal comes out too narrow, by roughly 0.35 to 0.5 times bend in relative SD (see the Accuracy section of inla_vanilla()).

  • Skew-normal fits. nmad, the largest gap between the fitted and the scanned density relative to its peak (flagged above 0.05), and sn_vs_vb, the gap between the skew-normal mean and the VB-corrected mean in posterior SDs. Both means target the posterior mean, so they should agree closely (to \(O(n^{-2})\); Jamil & Rue, 2026, Proposition 3.4). A gap above 0.1 SDs is flagged: the posterior is far from Gaussian along that parameter, and either approximation may be off.

  • Scan-end mass. scan_end_mass, the mass each fitted skew-normal puts outside the scanned window (the mode \(\pm 4\) Laplace SDs), where the marginal is extrapolated, as INLAvaan's diagnostics() reports it. A Gaussian marginal gives \(2\Phi(-4) = 6.3 \times 10^{-5}\); the larger it is, the more of the marginal is extrapolated. It is flagged above 0.05.

Some problems also raise one warning at the end of the fit, of class inlavanilla_diagnostics_warning: heavy tails, an NMAD above 0.1, a scan-end mass above 0.05, a VB shift above 1 SD or the VB fallback. These levels match INLAvaan's fit-time warning; the flags here are more sensitive. With silent = TRUE the warning is only recorded in fit$warnings. Printing the fit ends with a line for its warnings and one counting the checks flagged here, each shown only when there are any. vignette("diagnostics", package = "inlavanilla") explains every check with examples.

With vb = FALSE there is no VB mean, and the VB columns are left out. With marginals = "gaussian" there are no scans, so only the VB shift is reported.

References

Jamil, H., & Rue, H. (2026). Approximate Bayesian inference for structural equation models using integrated nested Laplace approximations (arXiv:2603.25690 [stat.ME]). arXiv. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2603.25690
